newsitem.title: USA: Toyota to build new coupe at Canadian plant.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to build new coupe at Canadian plant.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. said Wednesday it will launch production of an all-new coupe based on its Camry sedan next year at its Canadian assembly plant in Cambridge, Ontario.
Toyota expects to sell about 50,000 of the new coupes a year, mainly to aging baby boomers who lusted after coupes in the 1960s and no longer need family sedans or minivans.
The automaker showed a concept convertible version of the coupe called the Solara at the Chicago auto show, with proportions very similar to Chrysler Corp.'s Sebring JXi convertible.
But Toyota executives declined to say whether the production coupe will come in a convertible model or use the Solara name.
The car won't be called the Camry coupe, which it will replace in Toyota's lineup. The automaker does not intend to use the car to replace the Celica coupe, which is aimed at a younger audience.
Toyota is launching the new car at a time when coupes have fallen out of favor in the U.S. market as buyers in the baby-boom generation have shifted to sport utility vehicles, minivans and sedans.
Sales of small sporty coupes fell 16.6 percent in 1996 to 489,208 cars, according to J.D. Power & Associates.
But Don Esmond, a Toyota marketing executive, said the car would appeal to baby boomers who are no longer raising small children.

"There's an awful lot of lead boomers that we feel have a lot of fire in their gut for a good-looking coupe," he said. The Cambridge plant was upgraded for production of the coupe as part of a $480 million expansion in 1996, Toyota said.
The facility will have a combined capacity for the coupe and the Corolla sedan of about 200,000 cars a year, employing 2,200 people.
